statement: Let n = len(edges). For u and v with 0 <= u,v < n, dist(u,v) is the least integer k >= 0 for which there exist nodes w_0,...,w_k with w_0 = u, w_k = v, and for every j with 0 <= j < k, 0 <= w_j < n and edges[w_j] = w_{j+1}; dist(u,v) is undefined if no such k exists. A node x with 0 <= x < n is common iff dist(node1,x) and dist(node2,x) are both defined, and its cost is max(dist(node1,x), dist(node2,x)). The function returns a result r and the following holds. If some node x with 0 <= x < n is common, then 0 <= r < n, r is common, for every common x with 0 <= x < n cost(r) <= cost(x), and for every integer y with 0 <= y < r, either y is not common or cost(y) > cost(r). If no node x with 0 <= x < n is common, then r = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges). 2 <= n <= 100000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, -1 <= edges[i] < n and edges[i] != i. Also 0 <= node1 < n and 0 <= node2 < n.
